Direct Hill keys at LP2 page starts
nodes.question: Can any invertible direct 2×2 or 3×3 Hill matrix over the GP29 indices recover a fixed 12-rune known-reading opening at an LP2 page start?

scope.representation: First twelve recognized GP29 runes, including headings, from each of 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages.
scope.procedure: Split into consecutive 2- or 3-rune column blocks; test whether one invertible matrix maps all ciphertext blocks to one of nine fixed opening vectors. Verify dependencies and equal span rank; count rank-deficient invertible extensions.
scope.parameters: 2 block dimensions × 55 page starts × 9 openings = 990 complete-key feasibility cases over F29.
scope.exclusions: Unknown readings, later positions, shifted or reversed block origins, affine offsets, padding, transposition, nonlinear schedules and magic-square interpretations.

nodes.bounds: 2 block dimensions × 55 page starts × 9 openings = 990 complete-key feasibility cases over F29.
nodes.finding: Neither dimension two nor three admits an invertible direct block matrix for any of the 495 page-opening pairs. All 55 page starts have full ciphertext rank, so each candidate matrix is uniquely determined by its first independent blocks and fails on later blocks.
nodes.limitations: Only consecutive blocks from page origin zero, nine fixed openings, canonical GP29 arithmetic and one linear matrix per page are covered. Other plaintexts, offsets, affine rules, changing keys and transposition remain open.

nodes.label: Number panels as Hill-cipher keys
nodes.question: Do six pinned number-panel matrices, or the corrected LP2-15 panel, decode complete LP2 pages by fixed Hill blocks?

scope.representation: Source krisyotam GP29 rune indices: 55 nonempty unsolved page streams matching site text, plus their joined stream; LP2-50 is rune-free and omitted.
scope.procedure: Replay the pinned source, independently score all source matrices and a one-cell printed-panel correction, recover LP2-56 known reading under each operation, and repeat whole-grid selection on 199 shared pagewise shuffles.
scope.parameters: Six literal source matrices × four M/transpose/inverse/inverse-transpose operations × 56 targets = 1,344 outputs; one corrected 4×4 matrix × four operations × 56 targets = 224 outputs; modulus 29, block origin zero, final partial block dropped. The amended full-reading plant uses explicit zero padding removed after decoding.
scope.exclusions: Other matrices, block origins, affine offsets, key changes, plaintext languages, scoring models, interpretations of number panels and the unverified generation of the source phi variants.

nodes.bounds: Six literal source matrices × four M/transpose/inverse/inverse-transpose operations × 56 targets = 1,344 outputs; one corrected 4×4 matrix × four operations × 56 targets = 224 outputs; modulus 29, block origin zero, final partial block dropped. The amended full-reading plant uses explicit zero padding removed after decoding.
nodes.finding: The best source result scores -6.873 versus a −5.0 flag; its one-cell-corrected 4×4 arm scores at best -6.907. Zero outputs in either grid cross the flag. The complete known-reading plant recovers for all 28 operations; 146/199 and 69/199 complete shuffled searches equal or exceed the respective observed maxima.
nodes.limitations: This is a fixed-matrix, zero-origin, English-score test, not an exhaustive Hill search. The source discards incomplete final blocks, omitting 80 runes across the 4×4 page runs and 116 across the 5×5 page runs. The source’s 4×4 panel cell 820 differs from printed 1820; only that single-cell variant was retested. The source’s separate phi arrays are treated literally. Shuffled maxima are conditional order controls, not a cipher-generation probability.
